blocks.title: Network Appliances and Port Security comparison
Network Appliances and Port Security exam shortcuts
items: Admins need one controlled access point → JUMP SERVER
Example: Admins connect through a bastion host.
Need intermediary between clients and servers → PROXY
The proxy forwards requests on behalf of another system.
Example: A reverse proxy shields internal web servers.
Example: Inline IPS drops exploit packets.
Network access is granted after authentication.
Example: A laptop authenticates before the port opens.
EAP supplies the authentication method framework.
Example: Corporate devices use client certificates.
blocks.example: Focus on the exact requirement in the scenario before choosing the control.

questions.q: Administrators must access sensitive servers through one hardened intermediary host. Which device is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: A jump server provides a controlled administrative entry point.

questions.q: A device should alert on suspicious traffic but must not block it. Which control is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: An IDS detects and alerts without directly blocking.

questions.q: A device should detect and automatically block malicious traffic. Which control is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: An IPS actively prevents malicious traffic.

questions.q: A company wants users or devices authenticated before a switch port grants network access. Which technology is most relevant?
Corporate laptops use client certificates for 802.1X authentication. Which framework supports this?
questions.explanation: EAP provides authentication methods such as EAP-TLS for 802.1X.

questions.q: A company wants to distribute requests across several healthy web servers. Which device is best?
questions.explanation: A load balancer distributes client traffic across multiple servers.
